newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan watch firms enjoy higher interim profits.
newsitem.headline: Japan watch firms enjoy higher interim profits.

text.p: Japan's two leading watch companies reported a surge in their interim profits on Tuesday thanks to cost-cutting and the yen's decline against the dollar.

Seiko Corp said its parent current profit for the first half of the 1996/97 business year jumped almost 17-fold from a year ago to 1.15 billion yen ($10.3 million). However, sales fell 6.7 percent to 101.3 billion yen ($913 million).
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks.
Seiko produces wrist watches and jewellery, and its group firms make high-end timepieces.

Another major watch maker, Citizen Watch Co Ltd also saw profits surge. It reported a 40 percent rise for the six-month to 5.9 billion yen ($53.1 million). This was achieved despite a drop in sales, which fell 6.8 percent from a year ago to 100.4 billion yen ($904 million).

A yen decline against the dollar helps increase yen-denominated income and overseas sales. The yen has retreated sharply from postwar highs hit last year, and was trading at around 111 yen on Tuesday compared with a post-war high of 79.75 in April 1995.
"We were able to increase overseas sales significantly partly as a result of the yen's decline," a Seiko spokesman said.
The firm also made some foreign exchange profits in the first half, in addition to cutting costs, the spokesman said.
The company said that the decline in its sales was mainly due to its shifting of its loss-making domestic business in clocks to a subsidiary in July.
For the full year, Seiko expects to post 192 billion yen ($1.72 billion) in sales and 2.5 billion yen ($22.5 million) in parent current profit.
At Citizen, sales of wrist watches, the company's main product line, increased, but those of information equipment and parts, including notebook personal computers, fell.
"The company made utmost efforts to reduce costs," a company spokesman said.

In the area of information equipment and parts, the company moved some production operations overseas. It also placed emphasis on making more profitable models of printers than its mainstay dot-type printers.

The company revised down its forecast for full-year sales by around five billion yen ($45 million) to 200 billion yen. However, it also revised upward its full-year parent current profit forecast to 11 billion yen ($99 million) due to expectation of greater profitability. ($1=111 yen)
